catalog_quote: En este apartado mostraremos que la epéntesis vocálica en mazahua es producto de un requerimiento prosódico sobre el tamaño mínimo de la palabra fonológica: un pie trocaico silábico con el requerimiento adicional de que la sílaba prominente sea bimoraica. Mostraremos también que mientras los sufijos forman parte del pie, los clíticos no. ... La sílaba de la raíz (la tónica) y la del proclítico, por su parte, siempre manifiestan fonéticamente su tono léxico. ... [n.18] Cf. (15) con la regla de acentuación de Knapp (2008: 95) que no hace referencia a ningún tipo de estructura prosódica: “siempre se acentúa la primer sílaba del radical” ( Knapp 2008: 95). new_statements.rule_in_words: Mazahua is tonal; word stress falls on the initial syllable of the root (prefixes unstressed), and tone is contrastive only on that stressed root-initial syllable. Type also fits 'tone language with a stress statement'.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Alternating head-initial trochaic (secondary) stress reported for San Miguel Tenoxtitlán Mazahua (Knapp Ring 2008) and Depósito Mazahua (Juárez García & Cervantes Lozada 2005).
new_statements.identity_note: The failed work concerns the Temascalcingo variety (Mazahua de Temascalcingo). DiCanio & Bennett's statements rest on Knapp Ring 2008 (San Miguel Tenoxtitlán Mazahua, spelled 'Tenoxtitán' in the preprint) and Juárez García & Cervantes Lozada 2005 (Depósito Mazahua). Uchihara summarises Knapp 2015, which treats Mazahua generally and notes rising tone in 'some varieties'.

new_statements.translation: Michael Knapp's contribution, 'Tone-accent phenomena in Mazahua', reviews the history of studies of tone and stress in Mazahua [...] Knapp also explains that the basic melodic (metrical) structure of the base in this language is trochaic. [...] in the Otomanguean languages (Zapotec, Otomi, Mazahua, Ocuiltec and Ixcatec) [stress] is governed by morphological factors, such as the distinction between roots and suffixes. [...] Nahuatl, Mazahua, Otomi and Ixcatec have a trochaic pattern

new_statements.relation_note: Third-hand (a review's paraphrase of Knapp 2015), but consistent with DiCanio & Bennett: trochaic, root/base-initial stress in a tonal language; adds nothing contradictory.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is fixed and predictable, governed by morphology (root vs. affix); the base has a trochaic structure, i.e. prominence on the first syllable of the base; the language is tonal.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not discussed for Mazahua in the review; compounds noted as having two prosodic types (lexical vs. phrasal compounds) with different prosodic patterns.
new_statements.exceptions: Two compound types with different prosodic patterns (per Knapp 2015 as summarised).

Uchihara summarises Knapp 2015, which treats Mazahua generally and notes rising tone in 'some varieties'.
